patents.source: USPTO Open Data Portal, granted patents since 2001, applicant phrase "zoom communications", 2026-09-16

reading.body:
Zoom's AI Companion offers meeting summarization as a built-in feature, placing the company among the many existing software platforms adding LLM capabilities rather than building AI from the ground up.

Zoom's position differs from pure-play AI companies in a fundamental way: its value chain does not depend on new compute or power infrastructure. The company operates on existing video conferencing demand and adds AI Companion as a layer on top. This means Zoom's AI scaling does not face the binding constraint of grid capacity or the need for new data center buildings. It consumes compute on someone else's platform, likely cloud providers, in quantities proportional to user adoption rather than architectural ambition.

Meeting summarization and document generation are low-latency, episodic workloads unlike the continuous training or inference demands of frontier AI labs. Zoom's legal exposure in California, where it is headquartered, may relate to privacy and recording consent issues specific to capturing and processing meeting content, but the data does not specify which of 181 points of exposure apply to AI features versus core operations.

The data does not cover Zoom's compute spend, cloud provider agreements, or whether AI features drive material new infrastructure demand. It does not address whether Zoom generates derivative training data from summaries or whether it uses proprietary or third-party models for Companion.

profile_text.body:
Zoom is a public company traded under the ticker ZM, founded in 2011 and headquartered in San Jose, California. Its site describes it as one platform to connect, offering collaboration tools that include video meetings, Zoom Chat, VoIP phone, webinars, whiteboard, contact center, and events.

On AI, the company says built-in AI summarizes meetings and automates next steps, and that ZoomMate generates assets such as decks and docs. Its AI assistant product is Zoom AI Companion, which covers meeting summarization, a use for which recording consent is relevant.

The company's SEC Central Index Key is 0001585521. Its litigation record lists 281 cases in California.
